key_insight: Omni123 enables 3D-native foundation models to be trained despite scarce 3D data by unifying text→2D and text→3D generation in a shared framework, using abundant 2D supervision to bootstrap high-quality, geometry-consistent 3D synthesis.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of high-quality 3D assets and the under-constrained nature of text-to-3D generation; fixes reliance on indirect 2D-to-3D pipelines that produce inconsistent geometry by training a single 3D-native model with cross-modal supervision.
method: Unify text-to-image and text-to-3D generation within a shared model/latent space so 2D and 3D tasks provide mutual supervision.
Leverage abundant 2D data and pre-trained 2D generative models to distill visual knowledge into the 3D branch via cross-modal losses and multi-view consistency.
Use a 3D-native decoder/representation and synthetic renderings or limited real 3D assets to enforce geometric fidelity and reduce reliance on expensive 3D datasets.
impact: Enables practitioners to develop geometry-consistent text-to-3D systems with far less 3D data, accelerating downstream adoption in AR/VR, robotics, simulation, and content creation while lowering data collection cost.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing shared encoder, dual outputs (2D image branch and 3D branch), and cross-modal supervision arrows
Bar chart comparing data availability: abundant 2D vs limited 3D, illustrating the bootstrap effect
Schematic of multi-view / consistency loss (render → compare across views) to show geometry enforcement
paper_title: Omni123: Exploring 3D Native Foundation Models with Limited 3D Data by Unifying Text to 2D and 3D Generation
paper_authors: Chongjie Ye, Cheng Cao, Chuanyu Pan, Yiming Hao, Yihao Zhi
